The 52 books in 2027 challenge

3 min read · Updated: 24 November 2026

2027 has 53 Fridays, which makes it a good year for a book-a-week challenge: finish one book every Friday and you get one spare week for life getting in the way. Here is a month-by-month theme plan, the weekly rhythm and free tools to track it.

TL;DR
  • One book a week, finished by Friday; 53 Fridays give you one spare week.
  • Twelve monthly themes keep the list varied and the habit fresh.
  • Track it with our free online tracker or the printable sheet.

How does the 52 books in 2027 challenge work?

Read 52 books between 1 January and 31 December 2027, roughly one a week. 2027 starts on a Friday and has 53 Fridays, so if you aim to finish a book by each Friday you have a built-in buffer week. Pick books that fit each month's theme, tick each one off, and adjust the goal if it stops being fun.

The weekly rhythm

DayWhat to doTime
SaturdayChoose the week's book; read the first chapter30–60 min
Sunday to ThursdayRead on the commute or before bed35–45 min a day
FridayFinish, write three takeaways, tick it off10 min

That adds up to roughly 45 minutes a day for average-length nonfiction, less with audio during commutes. Our reading time calculator shows how long a specific book will take you.

A theme for every month of 2027

MonthFridaysThemeIdea
January5Habits and fresh startsStart with a short book you're excited about
February4MoneyOne budgeting book, one investing classic
March4Work and focusPair a deep-work book with a lighter one
April5PsychologyHow people think, decide and change
May4BiographyLives of founders, scientists, artists
June4Health and sleepCheck claims; talk to a doctor about personal decisions
July5Novels you've always meant to readSummer is for stories
August4Science and big ideasSpace, the brain, how we know things
September4Learning and languagesRead one book in a language you're learning
October5Leadership and peopleNegotiation, teams, conversations
November4HistoryOne era or region in depth
December5Free choice and rereadsReread your favourite of the year

How to make it to December

  1. Front-load January with short, gripping books to build the streak.
  2. Keep a short book on standby for chaotic weeks.
  3. Use your spare week before you fall behind, not after.
  4. Read with someone: a friend, a book club or a reading community.
  5. Lower the goal without guilt if it stops being enjoyable; 24 books is still a great year.

Where do summaries fit?

A 15–20 minute summary is a fast way to pick each week's book or to revisit one you finished, but it isn't the book itself. If you count summaries, keep them in a separate column so your 52 stays honest; the reasoning is in our 52 books a year guide. Questions people ask

When does the 52 books in 2027 challenge start?

It starts on Friday 1 January 2027 and ends on Friday 31 December 2027. Because 2027 has 53 Fridays, finishing one book each Friday gives you one spare week. You can join late: divide the books left by the weeks left and adjust the goal so it stays realistic.

How many minutes a day do I need for 52 books?

For average nonfiction of about 250 pages, plan on 40 to 50 minutes of reading a day, or around five hours a week. Listening to audiobooks on the commute or at the gym reduces the time you need to find at home. Longer or denser books push the daily time up.

Can I join the challenge with fewer books?

Yes. The same monthly themes work for 24 books (two a month) or 12 books (one a month). Choose the largest goal you can reach without dreading your reading time, and raise it mid-year if you're well ahead. Finishing 24 books you enjoyed beats abandoning 52 in March.

Is there a printable 52 books list for 2027?

Yes. Our printables page has a one-page 52 books sheet you can print or save as a PDF, along with a reading tracker and a book club starter kit. If you prefer to track online, the reading challenge tracker saves your ticks in your browser and shows whether you're on pace.
